hade-001.q: What seeded the region where Earth formed with heavy elements?
hade-001.a: A supernova shock wave in a dense part of the Milky Way.

hade-005.q: How did runaway accretion build Earth?
hade-005.a: Dust and debris from the solar nebula clumped into ever larger bodies.

hade-009.q: What was the Moon's first crust made of?
hade-009.a: Anorthosite, which separated from the magma below about 100 million years after the Moon formed.

hade-014.q: What do 4.4 Ga zircons show about Earth's crust?
hade-014.a: That it solidified about 100 million years after Earth formed.

hade-017.q: What sign of life do some Jack Hills zircons hold?

hade-019.q: In some models, what covered the Hadean Earth?
hade-019.a: A global ocean; models disagree on how much continental crust existed.

arch-001.q: Where is Earth's oldest known felsic crust?
arch-001.a: The Acasta Gneiss Complex in Canada's Northwest Territories, with zircons about 4.03 Ga.

arch-005.q: When is the final phase of the Late Heavy Bombardment placed?

arch-010.q: Where are the oldest known banded iron formations?
arch-010.a: At Isua, in Greenland's greenstone belt, about 3,800–3,700 Ma.

arch-013.q: From about when do anaerobic microbes appear?

arch-019.q: How large was the Wyoming Craton when it began?
arch-019.a: About 100,000 km², with gneisses of 3.6–3.0 Ga.

arch-021.q: What do the Barberton spherule layers record?
arch-021.a: At least four, and perhaps eight or more, impacts about 3.5–3.2 Ga.

arch-025.q: What do the Strelley Pool stromatolites suggest?
arch-025.a: Microbial communities reacting to shifting conditions about 3.43 Ga.

arch-029.q: When did the Zimbabwe Craton's Tokwe and Rhodesdale segments stabilize?

arch-034.q: When does evidence of oxygen-producing photosynthesisers appear?

arch-037.q: What reveals the Miralga impact structure?
arch-037.a: Shatter cones near Marble Bar in the Pilbara.

arch-041.q: What is the oldest known glaciation on Earth?
arch-041.a: The Pongola glaciation, about 2.985 to 2.837 Ga.

arch-046.q: When did the Abitibi greenstone belt form?

arch-050.q: When did the Slave Craton mainly stabilize?

arch-054.q: What was the first known Precambrian supervolcano?
arch-054.a: The Blake River Megacaldera Complex, begun about 2,707 Ma.

arch-061.q: What is notable about Sturgeon Lake Caldera?
arch-061.a: It is one of the world's best-preserved mineralized calderas, formed about 2.7 Ga.

arch-064.q: What was emplaced across the Zimbabwe Craton about 2.575 Ga?
arch-064.a: A 550 km band of layered ultramafic intrusions.

prot-003.q: What precipitated across most continents early in the Proterozoic?

prot-006.q: What irreversible change did free oxygen bring?
prot-006.a: It turned a weakly reducing atmosphere into an oxidizing one.

prot-009.q: What left the largest impact structure in India?
prot-009.a: An impact on the Bundelkhand craton.

prot-015.q: What has been proposed to have triggered the Makganyene snowball Earth?

prot-019.q: How are eukaryotes thought to have arisen?
prot-019.a: An Asgard archaeon took in an alphaproteobacterium.

prot-025.q: What formed the largest layered igneous intrusion in Earth's crust?
prot-025.a: Mantle magma rising through long cracks in the Kaapvaal crust.

prot-032.q: What did mountain building in Sweden, Finland and Russia do?
prot-032.a: It joined cratons of Baltica within Columbia.

prot-035.q: What did mountain building in Greenland form?
prot-035.a: The northern boundary of the North Atlantic craton.

prot-039.a: A coiled, tube-shaped fossil over a centimetre long.

prot-043.q: What formed the Trans-North China Orogen?
prot-043.a: Collision of the Eastern and Western Blocks of the North China Craton.

prot-049.q: What did the oldest ergs consist of?
prot-049.a: Sand seas, developed on several cratons.

prot-054.q: What collided with proto-North America in New Mexico and Arizona?

prot-059.q: What deposits formed during the Isan orogeny?
prot-059.a: Large lead, silver, copper and zinc deposits.

prot-063.q: When did Columbia begin to fragment?

prot-068.q: When did Africa's series of orogenic events end?
prot-068.a: About 1,000 Ma, when Rodinia was assembled.

prot-073.q: When did stromatolites reach their greatest diversity?

prot-075.q: Where was the Chuar Group laid down?

prot-083.q: What did the Warakurna province erupt?

prot-091.q: Which landmasses collided in the Rayner orogeny?

prot-096.q: What is called the 'Second Great Oxidation Event'?
prot-096.a: A rise in oxygen in the air and oceans c. 850–540 Ma.

prot-104.q: When did marine planktonic cyanobacteria first appear?

prot-110.q: How much area did magma flood in the Canadian Arctic and Greenland?
prot-110.a: More than 1.1 million km² in about two million years.

prot-114.q: What terranes were laid down as Sturtian glaciers retreated?

prot-120.q: What marks the start of the Ediacaran?
prot-120.a: The Nuccaleena cap carbonate above Elatina glacial deposits.

prot-124.q: What cycles do tidal rhythmites preserve?

prot-128.a: A mantle plume, the Central Iapetus Magmatic Province.

prot-132.q: How is the Gawler Ranges impact dated?
prot-132.a: By its ejecta in nearby basins, to about 590 Ma.

prot-136.q: What was the Avalon explosion thought to produce?

prot-140.q: What dates the Mistaken Point fossils?

prot-144.a: A large, slow-moving, quilted disc-like proarticulate.

prot-150.q: When did the Proto-Tethys Ocean exist?

camb-001.q: What marks the base of the Cambrian?
camb-001.a: A section at Fortune Head with the first Treptichnus pedum burrows.

camb-004.q: What did sea level do through the Cambrian?
camb-004.a: It rose gradually after a marine transgression.

camb-017.q: When do the first known footprints on land date to?

camb-028.q: When do trilobite body fossils first appear?
